slots.title: JOLTs openings consensus 7.13 million
slots.body:
September JOLTs — unfilled jobs employers report — posts at 3 p.m.
ET today.

Consensus: 7.13 million openings vs. 7.08 million last month.

Job quits (people leaving voluntarily): consensus 3.05 million vs. 3.07 million prior.

The survey is a labor-demand gauge the Fed watches alongside payrolls; ADP private payrolls for October follow tomorrow (consensus +65,000 jobs vs. +90,000 prior).

Prior session: Russell 2000 at 2,805.88 (−0.2%).

Which labor number matters more to you — openings or quits?

slots.title: US session recap — Nov. 3, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 closed down 0.5% at 7,541.40, off 38.67 points from the prior session, after trading between 7,539.38 and 7,662.23.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.1% to 25,164.36, a 272.63-point drop, with a session low of 25,145.95.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average bucked the broader decline, up 0.4% at 51,983.98, gaining 213.67 points.

The Russell 2000 slipped 0.2% to 2,805.88.

The VIX rose 8.9% to 21.15, up 1.73 points from a prior close of 19.42.

Technology was the weakest Nasdaq sector by average change, down about 3.5%.
Communication services averaged down 0.9%.
Energy averaged down 2.4%.
Consumer defensive averaged up 2.4%, the strongest sector print in the set.

Oracle led software stress among large caps: $ORCL finished down 8.9% at 119.10.
$AMD closed down 7.5% at 466.84 on a day it was on the earnings calendar with a 1.95 EPS estimate.
$MSFT fell 2.8% to 507.12.
$NVDA slipped 1.3% to 202.06.
$INTC was down 8.8% at 59.97 on heavy activity.

Regal Rexnord reported results in the earnings feed: EPS actual 3.74 versus estimate 2.65, with revenue actual about $524.6 million versus a much larger revenue estimate in the calendar line.

Consumer and payment names stood out to the upside:
- $WMT +3.4% to 127.69
- $HD +3.6% to 341.15
- $V +2.9% to 425.51
- $MA +3.1% to 658.10
- $PEP +2.2% to 140.42

Oil-linked products and majors weakened:
- $USO -7.1% to 156.87
- $XOM -4.0% to 179.67
- $CVX -3.3% to 227.77

Gold futures ($GCUSD) fell 0.8% to 3,937.00.
The dollar proxy ($UUP) was down 0.1% at 28.96.
Bitcoin ($BTCUSD) was flat at 76,686.53.

The economic calendar flagged US midterm elections and a 3:00 p.m.
Eastern slot for JOLTs job openings (September), with a 7.13 million estimate versus 7.079 million previous, plus job quits and an economic optimism index.

Treasury snapshot dated 2026-10-30 showed the 10-year at 4.9% and the 2s10s spread at 0.38 percentage points.

Overseas indexes were mixed ahead of or alongside the US close: FTSE 100 +0.3%, Hang Seng +0.4%, Nikkei 225 -0.3%.

slots.title: October jobs print due Friday at 8:30 a.m.
slots.body:
Nonfarm payrolls for October are scheduled for Friday, Nov. 6, at 8:30 a.m.
ET (13:30 in the calendar feed).

The median estimate is 65,000 jobs added; the prior release showed 29,000.

Private payrolls are estimated at 58,000 (prior 46,000).

The unemployment rate is estimated at 4.2%, unchanged from the prior 4.2%.

Average hourly earnings are estimated up 0.3% month over month and 2.9% year over year (prior 0.1% and 3.0%).

The report counts hiring across the economy and is the main monthly read on labor demand after a week of job-market surveys.

Which line do you watch first—headline payrolls, unemployment, or wages?
